passage: I'm Ayesha. My part of our group poster on birds was a mess: crooked lines and two spelling mistakes. When the bell rang I ran to catch my bus, but Keerthana stayed behind for another hour and redid it without saying a word about it. The next morning I saw the poster and my ears felt hot. I felt thankful and a bit guilty. I said, "Thank you, Keerthana. I'm sorry you had to stay. Next time I'll check mine first." She smiled. This week I finished my share early and helped her with the border.

qa.q: What was wrong with Ayesha's part of the poster?
qa.a: It had crooked lines and two spelling mistakes.

qa.q: What was Ayesha feeling when she saw the fixed poster?
qa.a: Thankful and a little guilty, and her ears felt hot.

qa.q: What could Ayesha do to keep the group healthy?
qa.a: Say thank you clearly and do Ayesha's own share carefully and on time, as Ayesha did this week.

qa.q: How might Keerthana have felt about staying behind?
qa.a: She did not complain and she smiled at Ayesha's thanks, so she may have been glad to help and glad to be noticed. 🙂

grounding: A group mate stays late to fix the child's part without complaint; the child feels grateful and guilty, says thank you and does their share next time.

passage:
In the school computer lab, Saurabh's part of the group presentation was a mess: wrong fonts, missing pictures, a spelling mistake in the title. He'd rushed it.
He left for the bus. Madhav stayed back for an hour and fixed it all. He didn't say a word about it in the group.
The next morning, Saurabh opened the file and saw. His cheeks went warm. He felt grateful, and a bit guilty.
He found Madhav at the gate. "Madhav, thank you. You fixed my slides. I should have done them properly."
Madhav shrugged. "It's fine."
"Next project, I'll do my part well. And I'll help you with yours."

qa.q: Where did Madhav stay back to fix the slides?
How did Saurabh feel when he saw what Madhav had done?
qa.a: He felt grateful and a bit guilty, his cheeks going warm.

qa.q: What did Saurabh do to repay Madhav?
qa.a: He thanked him clearly and promised to do his share and help next time.

qa.q: How might Madhav feel when Saurabh thanks him?
qa.a: Madhav may feel appreciated, even though he shrugs it off.

grounding: A group mate stays late to fix a boy's part without complaining; he feels grateful and a little guilty, thanks him clearly and promises to do his share.

passage:
Monday. Harsha's part of the group model, the cardboard bridge, kept collapsing. At home time he gave up and left.
Tuesday. When Harsha came in, the bridge was standing, strong and neat. Leela had stayed back after school and rebuilt it. She hadn't said anything.
Harsha felt thankful, with a twinge of guilt too. He had left it for someone else to fix.
Wednesday. Harsha found Leela at lunch. "Leela, thank you for fixing the bridge. I should have stayed."
She smiled. "It was fun, actually."
"Next time I'll do my part properly. And I'll bring you a mango from our tree."

qa.q: How did Harsha feel when he saw the bridge standing?
qa.a: He felt grateful and a little guilty for leaving it.

qa.q: What did Harsha do to show gratitude?
qa.a: He thanked Leela clearly and promised to do his part properly next time.

qa.q: How might Leela feel about fixing the bridge?
qa.a: Leela seemed happy, saying it was fun.

grounding: A group mate stays late to fix a boy's part; he feels grateful and a little guilty, thanks her clearly and promises to do his share.
